sink: onePanelAPI.uploadStaticFiles(domain, buildDirPath) -- uploads every file under buildDirPath to the operator's real 1Panel server, served publicly at http://{domain}
guard: partial: fs.existsSync(buildDirPath) only checks the path exists, not that it is within any allowed scope
why: buildDirPath is a caller-controlled absolute path with zero restriction on scope (the tool's own description invites arbitrary example paths). domain is also fully caller-controlled and is used to create/select a real website on the operator's actual 1Panel server. Combining the two: a caller can point buildDirPath at a sensitive local directory (SSH keys, credential files, application source) and domain at a name they can later resolve/reach, causing 1Panel to serve those files publicly over HTTP -- a genuine local-directory-exfiltration-to-a-public-webserver primitive, not merely 'deploy the project I built' since neither buildDirPath nor domain is constrained to the operator's intended project/site.

sink: fs.createReadStream(input) for any absolutePathCheck-passing image/mask path (content forwarded to OpenAI's API), and fs.writeFile(filePath,...) for file_output (same unrestricted write as create-image)
guard: bypassable: absolutePathCheck() only requires the string to start with '/' or a drive letter, with no extension gate and no directory containment at all
why: image/mask are read via fs.createReadStream(input) for ANY path that merely looks absolute -- unlike similar local-file-input tools elsewhere in this corpus, there is not even an image-extension gate (the extension is only used to guess a MIME type, defaulting to png for anything unrecognized). The file's raw bytes are then uploaded to OpenAI as the edit-source image, making this a genuine arbitrary-local-file-read-and-exfiltrate-to-a-third-party primitive. file_output has the same unrestricted-write issue as create-image.
contract: Absolute path to an image file (png, jpg, webp < 25MB) or a base64-encoded image string.
